proposals.rationale: Implemented PM/UserAdmin profile read returns active Developer availability, and no approved case covers this profile-detail contract; retain as a new atomic read case.
proposals.roleBoundary: Only an active PM with UserAdmin reads an active Developer profile; the profile exposes availability and readiness fields.
proposals.executionBoundary: Run against an isolated CAP SQLite fixture; assert the returned profile and no live catalog, BTP, or HANA mutation.
plannedAssertions: Read an active Developer and assert availabilityStatusCode, workloadLimit, readiness, and active responsibility count.
Assert the returned profile has no identity secret or unrelated user administration fields.

proposals.rationale: Active Developer targeting filters user.active=true and returns a safe not-found boundary; assignment denial does not prove profile-read secrecy, so retain a new negative case.
proposals.roleBoundary: Only an active PM with UserAdmin may request the profile read; an inactive Developer target must not yield profile data.
proposals.executionBoundary: Use an isolated in-memory CAP fixture with an inactive Developer; verify the safe rejection and unchanged database state.
plannedAssertions: Read an inactive Developer and assert the documented not-found status and error code.
Read back the fixture and assert no profile payload was exposed or changed.

proposals.rationale: The allowlist is implemented inside request validation, but no standalone role-check API returns a boolean; rewrite this row into one request-boundary matrix covering all allowed roles.
proposals.roleBoundary: Exercise the request validator with TESTER, DEVELOPER, and PM; UserAdmin overlay remains valid only for PM.
proposals.executionBoundary: Pure local contract invocation with no onboarding persistence, provider call, email, or live data mutation.
plannedAssertions: Assert all three business roles normalize and pass the request-access validator.
Assert an unknown role and a non-PM UserAdmin overlay are rejected with stable safe codes.

proposals.rationale: This is the same unbound role-allowlist branch as proposal 191, not a distinct Developer behavior; drop the duplicate row after the rewritten matrix covers the role set.
proposals.roleBoundary: No separate role boundary is retained; Developer remains covered by the single rewritten role matrix in Case 191.
proposals.executionBoundary: No new execution; preserve the source-only decision package and do not mutate onboarding or identity state.

proposals.rationale: This is the same unbound role-allowlist branch as proposal 191, not a distinct PM behavior; drop the duplicate row after the rewritten matrix covers the role set.
proposals.roleBoundary: No separate role boundary is retained; PM remains covered by the single rewritten role matrix in Case 191.
proposals.executionBoundary: No new execution; preserve the source-only decision package and do not mutate onboarding or identity state.

proposals.rationale: Catalog CREATE is implemented for ApplicationComponents behind the active PM/UserAdmin gate, while the approved catalog has no atomic component-create case; keep.
proposals.roleBoundary: Only an active PM carrying UserAdmin may create an Application Component; non-PM callers are rejected before persistence.
proposals.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP SQLite catalog fixture; assert normalized persistence and audit without touching canonical, BTP, or live data.
plannedAssertions: Create an Application Component as PM/UserAdmin and assert normalized code, name, active state, and audit.
Attempt the same create as a non-PM and assert HTTP 403 with no catalog row.

proposals.rationale: Catalog CREATE is implemented for DefectCategories behind the active PM/UserAdmin gate, while the approved catalog has no atomic category-create case; keep.
proposals.roleBoundary: Only an active PM carrying UserAdmin may create a Defect Category; non-PM callers are rejected before persistence.
proposals.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP SQLite catalog fixture; assert normalized persistence and audit without touching canonical, BTP, or live data.
plannedAssertions: Create a Defect Category as PM/UserAdmin and assert normalized code, name, active state, and audit.
Attempt the same create as a non-PM and assert HTTP 403 with no catalog row.

proposals.rationale: The catalog handler rejects non-PM callers before writes and the QA test exercises a TESTER rejection, but no approved case records this catalog authorization boundary; keep.
proposals.roleBoundary: TESTER, DEVELOPER, and other non-PM callers cannot create or update catalog entities; PM plus UserAdmin is required.
proposals.executionBoundary: Run an isolated catalog authorization test and verify no row or audit success event is created by a rejected call.
plannedAssertions: Attempt CREATE and UPDATE as TESTER and DEVELOPER and assert HTTP 403.
Read back catalog and audit fixtures to prove rejected calls did not mutate business state.

proposals.rationale: Source has two related boundaries: catalog parent activity and Bug classification bridge validation. The broad across-entities wording lacks a single assertion, so rewrite into explicit catalog versus classification cases.
proposals.roleBoundary: PM/UserAdmin catalog administration and authenticated Bug classification retain separate actor and entity boundaries.
proposals.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP fixtures for a catalog pair create and a Bug classification read/write; do not alter shared catalog or live data.
plannedAssertions: Assert a component-category create requires both active parents and rejects an inactive parent.
Assert Bug classification derives only an active bridge and rejects a missing or inactive bridge.

proposals.rationale: Inactive catalog values already follow the approved code-list rejection contract with HTTP 400 and no write; merge into the existing inactive-code case.
proposals.roleBoundary: The existing Bug classification validation boundary applies to every authenticated business role permitted to submit a Bug.
proposals.executionBoundary: Reuse the approved isolated validation fixture and assert HTTP 400 with no business write or side effect.

proposals.rationale: DeveloperWorkloads already counts non-Closed assigned Bugs per developer, exactly matching the active-bug dashboard assertion; merge into the open-count monitoring case.
proposals.roleBoundary: PM reads all workload rows; an active Developer is scoped to the row resolved from that Developer identity.
proposals.executionBoundary: Reuse the deterministic local workload fixture and assert aggregate counts without persistence or live dashboard mutation.

proposals.rationale: Monitoring computes overdue only from stored dueDate and today's UTC date; no configurable SLA threshold calculation is implemented, so rewrite the claim to a due-date boundary.
proposals.roleBoundary: PM monitoring may read the derived overdue flag; the test must not imply a separate configurable SLA service or Developer access.
proposals.executionBoundary: Use an isolated local fixture with due dates before, on, and after today; do not call external SLA or live monitoring systems.
plannedAssertions: Assert an open Bug before today is overdue while a Bug due today is not overdue.
Assert a CLOSED Bug remains not overdue and no SLA threshold calculation is claimed.

proposals.rationale: The workload reducer skips CLOSED rows and the approved monitoring cases already cover both overdue exclusion and open counts; merge into those exact cases.
proposals.roleBoundary: PM workload aggregation excludes CLOSED Bugs for every Developer row, while role authorization remains the existing monitoring boundary.
proposals.executionBoundary: Reuse isolated monitoring data and compare open counts before and after a closed row; no live Bug mutation is permitted.

proposals.rationale: DeveloperWorkloads scopes the actor before filters and the QA test proves own-row, profile-filter, search, and paging isolation; this authorization/read-model gap is not in the approved catalog, so keep.
proposals.roleBoundary: An active Developer can read only the server-resolved own workload row; PM can read the full workload model.
proposals.executionBoundary: Use deterministic local CAP workload fixtures and assert filter attempts cannot widen scope; no write or external access is involved.
plannedAssertions: Assert a Developer receives only the own row even with another-profile filter, search, offset, or count request.
Assert PM still receives the full ordered workload set.

proposals.rationale: The PM-only readBugStatusMetrics function is exposed with a PM requirement, but no approved case checks this function's Developer denial and sanitized no-payload boundary; keep.
proposals.roleBoundary: PM may call the status-metrics function; Developer and Tester calls must fail at the PM authorization boundary without metric payload.
proposals.executionBoundary: Run a local OData/CAP authorization contract with isolated status rows; do not query or mutate live monitoring data.
plannedAssertions: Assert PM receives the full current status metric set with zero-count rows preserved.
Assert Developer and Tester receive HTTP 403 and no status metric payload.
